title: feat(plugin-audit): the parent-record read gates write one ReadableIds leaf per parent object, with no pre-scan; D5's three classes keep the bounded probe (ADR-0139 E5)
body:
Fixes #23673

Clause-②: no

ADR-0139's row E5 (D4, D5): `plugin-audit`'s parent-record read gate stops pre-scanning. For every parent object the registry holds, it writes one `ReadableIds` leaf. D5's three classes are routed to the bounded probe, by name, before any leaf is written. #22788 remains open and keeps E6 and E7.

## What changed

`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/parent-record-read-gate.ts#computeParentRecordFilter`, shared by the activity stream's gate and the compliance ledger's gate:

- **The leaf (D4).** The parent objects are every registered object outside `AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS` and outside the gated object, plus the parents a gate declares (below). Each one gets the branch `{ object_name: P, record_id: { $in: ReadableIds.of(P) } }`, ORed together and ANDed into the read's `where`. The gate makes no engine call for a leaf. The engine composes it at its executor boundary, from the security service's `canReadObject` and `getReadFilter` for `P`, and the SQL drivers compile it to one tenant-walled subquery. A parent object the caller may not read is answered `$in: []` by the engine's own admission, without a caller-scoped read of it, so no denial is logged.
- **D5's classes keep the probe, decided up front from what the gate can see**, with no refusal caught:
  1. a delegated caller (`context.onBehalfOf.userId`, the engine's own test): the whole read goes to the probe;
  2. a parent an object-scoped read middleware narrows (`engine.hasObjectMiddleware(P)`);
  3. a parent bound to another datasource than the gated object (`engine.resolveEffectiveDatasource`). The comparison matches the engine's own binding comparison, or is stricter.
  The probe is today's mechanism, restricted to the rows that name those parents: a SYSTEM pre-scan bounded at 2,000, `canReadObject` first, then one caller-scoped read per parent object.
- **Two more whole-read probe states, each said once.** One is an engine that exposes none of those questions; all three are optional on their contracts. The other is a security service with no `canReadObject`, or no security service at all. On the second one, see "Measured" below.
- **The ledger's outside class is a predicate** (`ledgerRowAboutNoRecordWhere`): no record id, and an action that is not a record action. It is ORed in beside the parent branches, so the driver evaluates it with no bound. `isLedgerRowAboutNoRecord` stays as its in-process form.
- **The exemption capability is unchanged.** `view_all_audit_log` is decided before anything is enumerated, and nothing is written for its holder.
- **D3.** Neither consumer (`activity-read-visibility.ts`, `audit-log-read-visibility.ts`) wraps anything in a catch now. A leaf is composed after the gate's `next()`, so a composition or driver refusal is the read's own failure: it reaches the caller as `INTERNAL_ERROR` / 500 and is never turned into the deny-all sentinel. The probe's own fault is still answered deny-all inside the gate, and says so.
- **Interim letter C** never landed on `main`: ruling W on #22889 withdrew it, so there is no letter-C refusal to retire. What the leaf replaces is state D's warn-and-truncate.

### A reading of ADR-0139 D4 the reviewer should confirm

D4 enumerates parents "outside `AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS`", and also says rows "are excluded exactly as today". The ledger's auth-event sink writes `login` rows about `sys_session`, which is in that list (the CRUD mirror writes no row about a session). A member reads its own sessions under the `sys_session_self` policy, so today such a row is served when the session is readable. The ledger gate therefore names `sys_session` as a parent (`LEDGER_NAMED_PARENTS`, measured per writer), which keeps "exactly as today". The activity stream's only producer is the CRUD mirror, so for that stream the parenthetical is exact as written.

## Triage's own gate, read before the switch

`Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` on `main` after `462dff36f1`:
- first completed run: 38734785836 at `5477020809`, success;
- latest, per name: 38739002545 (push) and 38739484445 (schedule), both at `8d1fb1fb2d`, both success;
- the runs in between were cancelled or skipped, and none is red.

The job runs the whole `driver-sql` suite against both live servers, `sql-driver-readable-ids-conformance.test.ts` included, with `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1`.

## Measured

**On a real stack** (`bootStack`: the real `SecurityPlugin` and `AuditPlugin`, SQLite, org-bound). The fixture is a scratch dogfood file, deleted after the runs. It holds 5,042 owner-scoped records, 1,808 of them the member's, spread evenly. 5,054 activity rows are at rest, and the member may read 1,816 of them. The same fixture was read with the three gate files at the base `8d1fb1fb2d` and on this branch:

| reading | base | this PR |
|:--|:--|:--|
| member: list and `total` (truth 1,816) | 706 / 706 | 725 / 725 |
| administrator: `top=20&sort=-timestamp`, rows / `total` | 20 / 2,000 | 20 / 1,999 |
| ledger, member `total` (truth: 1,808 rows about its records, plus its own) | 691 | 1,819 |
| the gate's branches | 4 literal `$in` (701 ids on the owner-scoped object) | 53 leaves |
| a 2,000-id `id $in` in the final WHERE (the withheld-update rule) | none | 1 |

The ledger is served exactly. The activity stream is still capped, and the cap now comes from the withheld-update rule (`activity-field-redaction.ts#computeWithheldUpdateFilter`, ADR-0139 E6's). That rule pre-scans this gate's WHERE as SYSTEM, bounded at 2,000, and a `ReadableIds` leaf read as SYSTEM means "every id of P". So its window is the first 2,000 rows of the whole stream, whatever the reader may see. ADR-0139's consumer table (row 3) says that bound "caps the read even once consumer 1 is pushed down". The card's activity pins (1,808 of 1,808; an administrator's `total` of 4,201) therefore hold for this gate alone, as pinned below with the rule inert, and on a real stack only once E6 lands.

**The hazard the no-`canReadObject` state closes.** Withdrawing `canReadObject` from the real plugin-security makes the engine admit a leaf's parent by `explain`, and `explain` answers a SYSTEM context `allowed: false` (measured, `sys_user`), where `canReadObject` answers `true`. Leaves written in that state select nothing inside the withheld rule's SYSTEM pre-scan. The rule's `$nin` form then served the member two `sys_user` update rows whose every recorded change is withheld from it (6 rows against 4). Before this change that pre-scan read literal id lists, which mean the same thing under every context. So the gate writes no leaf without `canReadObject`.

**#22788 note 1, branch count and query time.** Shared-box readings; ratios are more meaningful than the absolutes.
- On the real stack above: 53 leaves. The member's `total` took 284 ms at base and 321 ms here, its page 262 ms and 284 ms, the administrator's top 20 438 ms and 390 ms.
- On the real-engine integration fixture: 2,606 rows, 8 branches (6 leaves and 2 probed). A member's find took 57.8 ms and its count 9.5 ms. The administrator's top 20 took 11 ms and its count 9.7 ms. The whole-read probe (a delegated caller) took 68.2 ms for find and 35 ms for count.

**Where the fixtures differ from the card's.** The card's 1,808 of 5,042 is report 6095496633's fixture at `1b99388505`: 13 parent objects and 2,540 distinct pairs. Here one owner-scoped object carries the bulk. The card's 4,201-row administrator store is not rebuilt separately; the administrator readings above are over 5,054 rows, and 2,606 in the integration suite.

## Pins, each ablated (old behaviour or the defect put back, red, restored)

Every mutation was made through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which checks the anchor count and the blob hash. The base-file swap was checked by hash against the `8d1fb1fb2d` blobs. Each restore was proven by `blob == HEAD` and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The dist-resolved legs (dogfood) took `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` readings on the pristine build, the mutated build and the restored build, the last with a clean tree.

| pin (file) | mutation | red |
|:--|:--|:--|
| past the window: a member's rows and `total`; an administrator's top 20 with a true `total`; the ledger served whole; the outside class as a predicate; one leaf per parent; the leaf reads no parent as the caller (`parent-record-read-leaf.integration.test.ts`) | the three gate files at the base | 9 of 14. The 5 that stay green are the control, the no-unreadable-row check, the delegated probe, and the holder |
| a non-holder's newest-first ledger page carries the rows about a record the old window never reached, on a real stack (`audit-log-audit-capability.dogfood.test.ts`) | the same, built into `dist/` | 1 |
| D5: a delegated caller is probed | the delegated routing deleted | 3. The engine refuses: "composes no such leaf for a delegated (on-behalf-of) caller" |
| D5: a middleware-narrowed parent is probed | never probed | 14. Engine refusals over `e5_gated` and `sys_comment_reaction` |
| D5: a federated parent is probed | never probed | 11. Engine refusals over `e5_far`, which is on `warehouse` |
| the exemption capability unchanged | the exemption line deleted | 5 |
| the outside class as a predicate | the predicate branch dropped | 14 |
| D3: a refusal raised by the read reaches the caller (a refusing-driver stand-in, as `driver-mongodb` refuses) | the consumer wraps `next()` and swallows | 2 |
| D3: the consumer catches nothing | the old compute catch put back, into deny-all | 1 |
| no leaf without `canReadObject` (`activity-withheld-update.integration.test.ts`, the silent-skip dogfood suite) | the guard deleted | 1 in the unit file, 1 integration (the withheld row is served), 3 dogfood |
| #23663's zero-denial pins, unchanged (`parent-record-read-admission.integration.test.ts`, `parent-read-gate-silent-skip.dogfood.test.ts`) | the probe's admission switched off | 7, and 3 in dogfood (four denial lines logged) |

The silent-skip dogfood suite passes with its text unchanged. The #23663 integration suite's stand-in gains `getReadFilter`, the other half the engine composes a leaf from. Its `asked` assertion now tells the gate's probe questions about the vault (the stripped envelope, unchanged) from the engine's composition questions about the board.

## Acceptance notes

- **The activity stream's broad read stays capped until E6** (above). E6 can carry this as a reading: the withheld rule's SYSTEM pre-scan composes the copied leaves for the system, so its window covers the whole stream. E6's predicate removes both. Carrier: E6 on #22788. Noted, not filed.
- **`explain` and `canReadObject` disagree on a SYSTEM context** in plugin-security (`explain` refuses, `canReadObject` admits). So the engine's composition of a leaf in a SYSTEM read selects everything or nothing, depending on which half the service offers. This PR guards its own consumer. Reach is measured only with `canReadObject` withdrawn, a contract-legal state that no in-tree service is in. Carrier: #22788 (the engine lane). Noted, not filed.
- **The engine composes each leaf with the outer read's full envelope**, operation-private keys included (`__readScope` stamped for the gated object). `core/src/security/operation-private-keys.ts` says an envelope forwarded to another object's question drops those keys. plugin-security re-stamps `__readScope` whenever it resolves sets, and otherwise denies, so no wrong answer was measured. Carrier: #22788. Noted, not filed.
- **On `driver-mongodb`**, both streams' reads now fail with 500, as ADR-0139's Consequences rule until O3. The Console's header bell and Home activity card would show an error on such a deployment.
- **The probe's "no candidate, nothing to narrow" shortcut is gone.** A read the probe finds no row for now stays narrowed, so a row written between the pre-scan and the read is judged rather than served. The rows served are otherwise unchanged.
- **By source reading only**, on a refusing driver the withheld rule's own catch would log "pre-scan failed, denying all" while the read still fails with 500 (the leaves stay in the final WHERE). Not measured on `driver-mongodb`. Carrier: E6.

## Tests and gates

Head `3ecca941d6`, after merging `main` at `c24598658d`:
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit test`: 50 files, 821 tests passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit typecheck`: exit 0.
- Dogfood: the 27 suites that read either gated object, once on this head, 27 files and 217 tests passed.
- The derived gate families: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, then `--ran`. The per-family readings are in the report on #23673. Every CI-run family is CI's to read on this PR.

## Changeset

`@objectstack/plugin-audit`: `minor`. Besides the ledger's truncation fix, a consumer on a driver that refuses the leaf observes a new failure mode: a read that served a capped list now fails with 500, as ruled. The published surface does not move (`Clause-②: no`): none of these modules is re-exported, and no input is newly accepted.
